title: Question 12
stem: Iodine-131 ($^{131}_{53}\text{I}$) is a radioactive isotope with a decay constant of $9.9 \times 10^{-7} \text{s}^{-1}$.

parts.label: (a)(i)

markscheme_points.text: emits ionising radiation or decays spontaneously

hints: Hint 1: Think about what is different inside the nucleus of this isotope compared to a stable isotope - is it about the balance of forces holding it together?
Hint 2: What does such an unstable nucleus do on its own, without any outside push, and what does it give out when it changes?
parts.proper_answer: Radioactive means having an unstable nucleus that decays spontaneously with the emission of ionising radiation.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **What unstable means**
Think of a nucleus as held together by a delicate balance. In iodine-131 the neutron to proton ratio makes it unstable, so it cannot stay as it is forever.

Step 2: **What it does**
Left entirely alone, it will spontaneously break up or rearrange to become more stable. In doing so it emits ionising radiation such as alpha, beta or gamma radiation.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
hints: Hint 1: Remember decay is random for one nucleus but predictable for many - so the decay constant must be a chance or likelihood idea, not a fixed number decaying per second.
Hint 2: Check the unit given in the stem, $\text{s}^{-1}$. What phrase with the word per unit time would give that unit?
parts.proper_answer: The decay constant is the probability of decay of a nucleus per unit time.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Probability, not rate**
You cannot say when one particular iodine-131 nucleus will decay. You can only talk about the chance it decays in the next second. That is why $\lambda$ is defined as a probability.

Step 2: **Per unit time**
So $\lambda = 9.9 \times 10^{-7} \text{ s}^{-1}$ means each nucleus has a probability of $9.9 \times 10^{-7}$ of decaying in each second. The full definition is probability of decay of a nucleus per unit time.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Some water becomes contaminated with iodine-131.
The activity of the iodine-131 in $1.0 \text{kg}$ of water is $560 \text{Bq}$.

Determine the number of iodine-131 atoms in $1.0 \text{kg}$ of water.
hints: Hint 1: Activity in becquerel tells you how many nuclei decay per second. How must this be linked to the total number present $N$ and the chance per second for each one?
Hint 2: Rearrange that link to make $N$ the subject, then check that $1 \text{ Bq} = 1 \text{ s}^{-1}$ so the units work out to a pure number.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Link activity to number of nuclei**
Activity is the rate of decay. More nuclei means more decays per second, and larger $\lambda$ means larger chance per second. Together:
$$A = \lambda N$$

Step 2: **Rearrange and substitute**
Make $N$ the subject:
$$N = \frac{A}{\lambda}$$
$$N = \frac{560}{9.9 \times 10^{-7}}$$
$$N = 5.7 \times 10^{8}$$
This is the number of iodine-131 atoms in 1.0 kg of water.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Regulations require that the activity of iodine-131 in $1.0 \text{kg}$ of water is to be less than $170 \text{Bq}$.

Calculate the time, in days, for the activity of the contaminated water in (b) to be reduced to $170 \text{Bq}$.
hints: Hint 1: Activity does not fall at a steady rate, it falls by the same fraction in equal times. Which exponential law links present activity $A$ to initial activity $A_{0}$?
Hint 2: You know $A$, $A_{0}$ and $\lambda$. How can you undo the exponential to get $t$ out of the power - think about taking logs on both sides?
Hint 3: Your $t$ from the equation will be in seconds because $\lambda$ is in $\text{s}^{-1}$. What factor will you divide by to give the answer in days?
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Use the exponential decay law**
Activity follows the same exponential fall as number of nuclei:
$$A = A_{0}e^{-\lambda t}$$
Here $A_{0} = 560 \text{ Bq}$ and $A = 170 \text{ Bq}$.

Step 2: **Substitute and solve with logs**
$$170 = 560 \exp(-9.9 \times 10^{-7} \times t)$$
$$\frac{170}{560} = e^{-\lambda t}$$
Take natural log:
$$\ln\left(\frac{170}{560}\right) = -\lambda t$$
$$t = \frac{-\ln(170/560)}{9.9 \times 10^{-7}}$$
$$t = 1.2 \times 10^{6} \text{ s}$$

Step 3: **Convert seconds to days**
$$t = \frac{1.2 \times 10^{6}}{86400} \text{ days}$$
$$t \approx 14 \text{ days}$$
So after about 14 days the activity falls below 170 Bq.
